# Developer Handbook — AI-Driven Trade Surveillance for Market Abuse — Developer Handbook

> Everything a developer needs from first commit to pilot launch.

---

## PART 1 — EPICS & USER STORIES

### EPIC 1: Foundation & API Scaffold
**Goal:** Any developer can clone the repo and call the API within 10 minutes.
**Points:** 13

#### Story 1.1 — Project scaffold and solution structure (3 pts)
**As a** developer
**I want** the solution structure created with correct project references
**So that** I can start building without wondering where code belongs

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Solution builds with zero warnings
- [ ] `dotnet run` starts API at `http://localhost:5000`
- [ ] `GET /api/health` returns HTTP 200 with status "healthy"
- [ ] All NuGet packages pinned (no floating versions)
- [ ] README documents setup in under 5 steps

#### Story 1.2 — LLM provider cascade wired (5 pts)
**As a** developer
**I want** the multi-model cascade functional with offline fallback
**So that** the app works without API keys configured

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Gemini → Groq → Claude cascade order verified
- [ ] Heuristic engine returns domain-appropriate data offline
- [ ] `modelUsed` field correctly reflects which provider responded
- [ ] SSE `/api/events/model-status` stream emits `attempting`/`succeeded`/`failed` events
- [ ] Circuit breaker opens after 50% failure rate over 30s

---

### EPIC 2: Research & Domain Intelligence
**Goal:** User can enter keywords and receive prioritised AI solutions with competitor insights.
**Points:** 21

#### Story 2.1 — Research endpoint (8 pts)
**As a** user
**I want** to submit industry keywords and receive ranked AI solution opportunities
**So that** I can identify the highest-value use cases to pursue

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Returns exactly 5 items and 4 competitor insights on page 1
- [ ] Items include `urgency`, `difficulty`, `value` scores (1–10)
- [ ] `loadMore: true` returns 5 additional items not in `existingItemIds`
- [ ] `isRerun: true` evicts cache and regenerates
- [ ] Response cached for subsequent identical queries
- [ ] Works offline via heuristic engine for all 9 supported verticals

---

### EPIC 3: Blueprint Generation
**Goal:** Selected solution generates a full architectural blueprint with topology and schema.
**Points:** 13

#### Story 3.1 — Blueprint generation (8 pts)
**As a** developer
**I want** to generate a system blueprint from a selected solution
**So that** I have a concrete architecture to build from

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Returns `coreScenario`, `baseTopology`, `databaseSchemes`, `endpointManifest`, `resilienceStrategies`
- [ ] All fields are Markdown strings (300+ words for `coreScenario`)
- [ ] Blueprint cached for 24 hours per `(solutionId, solutionName, domain)` key
- [ ] ASCII topology diagram present in `baseTopology`
- [ ] SQL DDL present in `databaseSchemes`

---

## PART 2 — ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW

```
MeridianStudio.API/
├── Domain/           ← Models, no dependencies
├── Application/      ← Services, contracts, orchestration
├── Infrastructure/   ← LLM providers, local engine, guard, cache
└── API/              ← Minimal API endpoints, program bootstrapping

MeridianStudio.UI/
├── core/             ← Services, models, tokens, pipes
└── features/         ← Standalone Angular components per workspace tab
```

**Dependency rule:** `Domain` ← `Application` ← `Infrastructure` ← `API`.
No upward references. UI `WorkspaceStoreService` is the single state hub.

---

## PART 3 — COMPONENT REFERENCE

| Component | Purpose | Key Responsibilities | Does NOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WorkspaceStoreService` | Single Angular state hub | Holds all signals, calls all HTTP endpoints | Contain business logic |
| `LocalCompilationEngine` | Offline AI fallback | Returns domain-aware heuristic data for all endpoints | Call any external API |
| `PromptBuilder` | Prompt construction | Builds (system, user) prompt pairs per endpoint | Execute LLM calls |
| `InputGuard` | Input validation | Validates, sanitises, blocks injection patterns | Log or modify domain data |
| `ProjectGeneratorService` | Zip generation | Builds complete project zips for 5 languages | Make LLM calls |

---

## PART 4 — ABSTRACTION MAP

| Third-Party | Interface | Production | Fallback |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gemini API | `ILLMOrchestrator` | `GeminiProvider` | `LocalCompilationEngine` |
| Groq API | `ILLMOrchestrator` | `GroqProvider` | `LocalCompilationEngine` |
| Claude API | `ILLMOrchestrator` | `ClaudeProvider` | `LocalCompilationEngine` |

**Swap pattern:** Change one DI registration in `Program.cs`. All service classes unchanged.

---

## PART 5 — DESIGN PATTERNS

| Pattern | Where | Why chosen |
|---|---|---|
| Cascade + Circuit Breaker | `LLMOrchestrator` | Maximises uptime; single fallback eliminates total outage |
| Signals (Angular) | All UI components | Eliminates `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` boilerplate; reactive without RxJS overhead |
| Repository pattern | `WorkspaceStoreService` | Centralises state; components never call `HttpClient` directly |
| Raw string literals | `PromptBuilder.cs` | Readable multi-line prompts without escape-character noise |
| Heuristic offline engine | `LocalCompilationEngine` | Zero external dependencies in CI/CD; deterministic test data |

---

## PART 6 — TO-DO CHECKLIST

### Week 1 — Foundation
- [ ] `dotnet build` passes with zero warnings
- [ ] `npm start` serves Angular at `http://localhost:4200`
- [ ] `/api/health` returns healthy JSON
- [ ] LLM cascade verified with real API keys
- [ ] Offline heuristic engine verified without API keys

### Week 2 — Research & Blueprint
- [ ] Research returns 5 items for all 9 domain verticals
- [ ] Blueprint generates for any selected solution
- [ ] SSE model status stream emits events for each API call

### Pre-Launch Checklist
- [ ] All API keys configured via `dotnet user-secrets`
- [ ] CORS policy updated for production origins
- [ ] Cache TTLs reviewed and set appropriately
- [ ] No hardcoded credentials in any committed file
- [ ] `GET /api/health` returns healthy in production environment
